questions.q: What do --allow-blob-public-access false and --default-action Deny do together on an Azure storage account?
options: Allow public read access but block write access
Delete the storage account's existing containers
Turn off anonymous public read access and make the account's firewall deny every request by default until a rule allows it
Have no effect unless a VNet is also attached
questions.explain: Together they set the account to deny-by-default with no anonymous public read, requiring an explicit rule to allow any access.

questions.q: What does the az storage account network-rule add call in this lesson's example actually do?
options: Opens exactly one path in — traffic from a specific VNet/subnet — rather than opening broad access
Deletes the default-deny firewall rule entirely
Creates a new storage account
Grants public read access to everyone on the internet
questions.explain: The network rule is a scoped exception to the default-deny posture, allowing traffic from one named subnet only.

questions.q: Does aws s3api create-bucket make a new bucket publicly accessible?
options: Only if a region is specified
Yes, every new bucket is public by default
Only for buckets created outside us-east-1
No — new buckets already default to private, but that alone doesn't guarantee a later policy or ACL won't open it
questions.explain: New buckets default to private, but create-bucket alone provides no guarantee against a future permissive policy or ACL.

questions.q: What does put-public-access-block with all four settings set to true guarantee?
options: The bucket is deleted if it's ever made public
Only AWS support can read the bucket's contents
The bucket becomes permanently read-only
No ACL, bucket policy, or cross-account grant can make the bucket or its objects public, regardless of later configuration
questions.explain: Block Public Access settings override any ACL or policy that might otherwise make the bucket public, as a standing guarantee.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should happen after a storage account or bucket is locked down to deny-by-default?
options: Public access should be re-enabled so the application can reach it
A later, separate step grants a specific, scoped access to only the identity or network that actually needs it
The storage account should be deleted and recreated without deny-by-default
Nothing further is needed — the storage is now fully usable
questions.explain: Locking down first and then opening exactly one scoped path is the deliberate two-step order this lesson teaches, completed in Lesson 11.
